ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Boston show with stellar Saint Stephen and soaring China>Rider
ai_show_review.blurb: The April 7, 1971 performance delivers a blistering Saint Stephen and a seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition. Highlights include a hard‑rock Hard To Handle and an explosive post‑drums Not Fade Away jam. The Betty Cantor soundboard capture is crystal clear and showcases the band at full tilt.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Boston Music Hall on April 7, 1971 finds the Dead in top form, riding a high‑energy wave that never loses its momentum. The first set builds with tight rock numbers—Me And My Uncle, Casey Jones and a punchy Hard To Handle—setting up a second‑set launch that kicks off with an immaculate China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue. From there the band rockets into a smoking Saint Stephen where Phil’s bass rumbles like a plant being pulled from its pot and Jerry’s plug‑in guitar pierces the mix with crystal‑clear leads. The drum duo erupts into a thunderous segment that segues into an unforgettable Not Fade Away jam, building to an intense climax before the tape cuts short. Throughout, Brent’s (Pigpen’s) organ adds subtle texture while Bill Kreutzmann drives the rhythmic foundation with precision. This show is captured on Betty Cantor’s renowned soundboard tape, which delivers exceptional clarity and balance, making it one of the standout April ’71 documents.

best_recording.reason: Betty Cantor soundboard tape with excellent clarity, crisp guitar plug‑in and high‑energy performance; considered the premier source for this show

key_highlights: Smoking Saint Stephen with rumbling Phil bass and soaring Garcia leads
Seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition that launches a blazing second set
Epic post‑drums Not Fade Away jam building to an intense climax (though cut short)
Hard‑rock Hard To Handle delivering tight groove and vocal fire

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s plug‑in guitar shines, delivering crisp leads on Saint Stephen and driving the post‑drums jam with inspired phrasing.
band_performance.Phil: His bass on Saint Stephen is a classic ‘Phil bomb,’ rumbling powerfully beneath the band’s high‑energy flow.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann anchors the rhythm, with the drum segment highlighted as a standout moment that propels the Not Fade Away jam.
